ICS:
Allows colleague to express self
(does not interrupt, expresses interest in hearing more, asks how pt/parent feels)

Communicates in non-judgmental fashion
(no leading questions, is respectful and courteous, no patronizing or arrogant comments)

Makes empathic and supportive statements
(expresses concern, acknowledges emotional content and/or coping efforts)

Uses language appropriate to situation
(using terms that are unambiguous but not offensive)

Uses non-verbal behavior that is facilitative & culturally appropriate
(appropriate distance, tone of voice, attentive posture, gestures & verbal message match)

Proceeds in organized fashion
(clear beginning, middle & end, moved through encounter in efficient manner)

Clearly state your concerns
(Your behavior was not appropriate)

Be specific about the behavior - not the person
(e.g.  "your comments were impatient" vs. "you were terrible")

Elicit self assessment
(What did you think of your behavior?)

Acknowledge resident stress
(I know there's too much work to do)

Remain neutral  in face of anger
(Doesn't get angry at resident)
PROF:
Explain your rationale
(The behavior of one person represents the whole medical center / profession. We need to work together as a team. The patient is the priority)
